div.head: III Atr 8
div.ab: And ælc mynetére, þe man tihð, þæt fals feoh sloge, syððan hit forboden wæs, gange to þrimfealdan ordale; gif he ful beo, slea hine man.
Et omnis monetarius qui accusabitur, quod falsum fecit, postquam interdictum fuit, adeat triplex ordalium; si culpabilis sit, occidatur.
And ælc mynetére þe man tihð þæt fals feoh sloge, syððan hit forboden wæs, gange to þrimfealdan ordale; gif he ful beo, slea hine man.
Und jeder Münzer, den man verklagt, dass er, seitdem es verboten worden war, falsches Geld geschlagen habe, gehe zu dreifachem Ordal; wenn er schuldig erfunden ist, werde er hingerichtet.
And every moneyer who is accused of having struck false coin since it was forbidden, let him go to the threefold ordeal; if he is found guilty, let him be killed.
And every moneyer who is accused of striking false coins, after it was forbidden, shall go to the triple ordeal; if he is guilty, he shall be slain.
And every moneyer who is accused of coining false money, since it was forbidden, is to go to the three-fold ordeal; if he is proved guilty, he is to be slain.

note.seg: Vgl. Gl ‘verlorene Gesetze’ 14. Nicht gemeint sein kann II As 14, 1, weil kein Münzer länger als 60 Jahre arbeitete. Möglicherweise ein Gesetz von ‘Bromdun’; o. 4
Cf. Gl ‘verlorene Gesetze’ 14. II As 14, 1 cannot be meant, because no moneyer worked for longer than 60 years. Possibly a law of ‘Bromdun’; above 4
For other corporal punishments see ibid. 7

The only previous reference in the laws which have come down to us is in II As. 14, 1. As over half a century must have elapsed since that time, it seems probable that the reference is to a lost law; cf. the references to a council at Bromdun, I Atr. 1, 2; III, 4.
